title: Changing times and violence
summary: Opinions on gossip, young people and a killing in the paper.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Yeah, boy, Lord. You tell my door poppers is in them white neighborhoods now. They talk about door poppers. They'll be peeping. You don't know they peeping. Watching everything. They watch each other's business more than we do. But they're afraid to come out and talk about each other like we do because they can be sued. They got something to lose. We don't have anything to lose. And we just talk, run off the mouth. But they got something to lose. And they'll sit down and talk together. But they say, now don't you mention I said it. Don't call my name. They have them parted and things. I don't know. Everything has changed now. Everybody's changed. The young people is more wicked and more ruthless and want to kill. I read in the paper yesterday. The little boy said kill for fun. Stuck a knife and will go back and say kill for fun. Now, they'll send him to some place and say he's insane. When he gets to be a grown man, he'll come out and might kill again. That's in it. You got to keep him there for life.
That's what they need to do.

It's just like the little boy here that killed the other one, the school boy. He's in there talking about he's insane. That boy ain't been more insane than I am. He took that boy and that boy might have had some money carrying him down to say the child was attacked. And he about attacked him and killed him because he know the boy is going to tell him. He had sense enough to catch the train and go away, didn't he? Yeah. Well.
